commit: see git log of the branch (this file is committed with the work it describes)

requirements.notes: 21 admitted structural training families (all ten Part 7.4 checks on seeds 0-2, fingerprint-distinct); 19 also pass on held-out seeds 10-12. Below the 60 required; the next wave adds families (generator recipes and the four remaining engines).
7 admitted families in the new partition v5-eval-1 (8 registered; net_cascade fails difficulty). 4.0's 18 val/test families are untouched and not counted. Below the 20 required.
All ten categories 8.1-8.10 have admitted families.
8 independent engines with families: 5 v5 engines (no engine module imports another) plus the preserved 4.0 scm, abm, techsys.
Every family has a measured nine-component fingerprint (motifs, motif edges, topology, temporal, observation, action interface, objective, participants, engine); registry entries carry it.
All ten action kinds are offered by admitted families.
29 families feasibility-validated (consistency, conservation, oracle achievability on every seed), 0 admitted without it. The count criterion (80) needs more families.
29 families with intervention tests, 87 runs on 3 seeds, 0 failures; the look-alike markets are told apart by one protocol. The count criterion (80) needs more families.
A renamed copy and a parameter variant of every family have distance 0 and are not counted (0 of 58); minimum distance between registered families 0.063.
28 versioned primitives with parameter schemas, vectorised implementations and passing characteristic-behaviour experiments; versions enforced.

4 of 8: discrete-event, graph dynamical, search/information, partially observed state machine. Executable program, multi-agent strategic, scientific experiment and planning/resource engines are the next wave.
Ten checks, each rejecting a broken control world; 0 oracle exposure findings (static isolation, 852 hidden numbers scanned, kernel tool outputs).

Ten Part 8.11 action types offered by admitted families and each shown to have its effect on a real world (tool discovery = query target 'tools' and a catalogue that grows the action space; programs run in the sandbox).
Nine difficulty axes, each measured to change the world; 0 mismatches between the fast simulators and kernel-hosted rig twins (320 ticks, 4 families, 3 engines) and between batch and single worlds.

limitations: Gate M counts are below threshold: 21/60 training, 7/20 evaluation, 29/80 feasibility-validated and intervention-tested families; SP-7.3 has 4 of 8 engine kinds.

Families were tuned against admission seeds 0-2; on held-out seeds 10-12, des_bottleneck and dl_short_term_damage fail the difficulty check (26 of 29 admitted there). net_cascade fails on both seed sets and is not admitted.
The difficulty check uses scripted public-information references; a weak reference can fail a family that is not too hard. Oracles are search-based references on realised noise, not proven optima.

RapidEnv cash is unconstrained (may go negative); only the 4.0 lever view and the rig twin apply 4.0 money rules. Structured-action families have no kernel module yet (kernel twin only for lever families through rig).
The informativeness check shows observations depend on the hidden instance (variance ratio, hidden-state predictability), not that any learner can exploit them.
integration_notes: Importing crucible.rapid.mechview registers a 4.0 mechanism engine named 'rapid' in crucible.mechanisms.base.ENGINES; it adds no MECH_FAMILIES entries, so 4.0 family lists, splits, tasks and sealed sets are unchanged (test_mech_rig's every-engine test skips engines without families).
No kernel module was added (no rapid/modules.py); load_all_modules is unaffected.

Admission results are cached under $CRUCIBLE_CACHE/rapid/ keyed by a digest of the rapid sources; delete to force recomputation. Gate tests run admission on seeds 0-2 and 10-12 (about 60 CPU-s each) and are marked slow; run them through crucible.scale.slots.

The Observation dict follows INTERFACE_CONTRACTS section 11 field for field (crucible.rapid.observation.FIELDS); workstream L's ExperienceEnv can wrap Env directly (observe/step/observe_since/tools/outcome).

crucible.rapid.fingerprint(family) and crucible.rapid.admit(family, seeds) are the contract functions; the fingerprint module is crucible.rapid.fingerprints (plural) so the function name is not shadowed.
No packages were installed; numpy only (torch is used by one test through the existing ppo_gru learner).
